sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Lòkə́ə Phonology' (pp. 24-104) treats suprasegmentals only as tone: section 2.12 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 54-60) = two tonemes H and L (plus a mid tone restricted to bitonal combinations on long syllables), section 2.213 long-syllable tones, 2.42124/3.317 nominal tone patterns, 2.5 (p. 97ff) downdrift as the phrase-level intonation. The words 'stress'/'accent' never occur in a prosodic sense anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned layer; 'accent' only for the acute/grave diacritics). Describes the Ugep (Lòmòmò) dialect.

sources.note: Background section 2 only: 'Lokạạ operates a 2-tone system: high and low. Tones in Lokạạ have both lexical and grammatical functions.. The contour tones on long vowels are not phonemic but rather a combination of phonemic low and high tones (IWARA et al. 2003).' Nothing on stress. Data from the Ekuri dialect.
